actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: Environment is a gym.Env subclass and its docstring calls it an OpenAI Gym-style environment class
The constructor's default control frequency is hz=240 and p.setTimeStep(1. / hz) sets the simulation timestep from it
The action space is a Dict with pose0 and pose1; each is a Tuple of a 3-vector position bounded low [0.25, -0.5, 0.] and high [0.75, 0.5, 0.28] and a 4-vector orientation bounded -1.0 to 1.0
The observation space is a Dict of color and depth Tuples, one entry per camera; color is 0..255 uint8 and depth is 0.0..20.0 float32
The environment uses three RealSense D415 cameras declared with image_size (480, 640)
EnvironmentMCTS.step treats pose0 as the PICK pose and pose1 as the PLACE pose and returns [pick_obs, place_obs], reward, done, info
EnvironmentMCTS.reset resets the task, calls step() with no action, and returns the 6-tuple (init_obs, base_urdf, base_size, base_id, objs_id, info)
demos_tvf.py defaults --task to put-block-base, builds tasks.names[task + '-mcts'], and runs EnvironmentMCTS with hz=480
The task registry maps 'put-block-base-mcts' to PutBlockBaseMCTS
PutBlockBaseMCTS has 3 blocks, a stand base of size (0.05, 0.15, 0.005), three place positions on the base, and max_steps = num_blocks + 2
PutBlockBaseMCTS appends one goal with its object list and max_reward 1
TaskMCTS.reward adds max_reward / len(objs) to step_reward
TaskMCTS.done returns true when no goals remain or the accumulated reward exceeds 0.99
Environment.seed sets a numpy RandomState for the environment's random generator and returns the seed
The reset loads a UR5 arm with a suction end effector and moves its joints to the home configuration
The put-block-base task's workspace bounds are x 0.25..0.75, y -0.25..0.25 and z 0..0.28

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's initial block layout and every transition is deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws with Python's random.Random while upstream Environment.seed uses numpy's RandomState, so the two do not produce the same scene for one seed

gaps: analytic kinematic pick-and-place: block poses are updated directly, with no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, suction, actuator, sensor or noise model, and the UR5 arm is not simulated
the fake models only the demo's default put-block-base-mcts task (3 blocks, 3 target positions) and not the other 13 MCTS task classes in the registry
the fake's observation is an 8x8 placeholder colour/depth image per camera, not the upstream 480x640 (cameras.py:26) RGB-D render, and its values are test data, not sensor measurements
the fake samples block poses uniformly inside the task bounds instead of upstream's collision-free get_random_pose over the rendered free-space mask, and it ignores pose orientation when matching
the fake uses Python random.Random, upstream Environment.seed uses numpy RandomState and the demo script seeds the global np.random (demos_tvf.py:50), so one seed gives different scenes on the two
the SDK's legacy reset path serves only the first element of the native 6-tuple: base_urdf, base_size, base_id and objs_id are not carried in the reset receipt

cap.world.reset.v1 advertises an options object, but the native reset(self) accepts neither options nor a seed keyword; the bridge's legacy fallback calls env.seed(seed) and then reset() and drops options

the action space is the base Environment space (y -0.5..0.5) because EnvironmentMCTS overrides position_bounds after the base __init__ without rebuilding action_space; the task's own workspace bounds are y -0.25..0.25 (put_block_base_mcts.py:44)

the package's pose adapter supplies numeric tuple schemas and source-backed coordinate and quaternion bounds that the generic bridge does not derive; an out-of-envelope pose is refused before native dispatch, rather than treated as a fake timeout

a live EnvironmentMCTS requires assets_root and a configured task, opens a PyBullet client and loads plugins during construction; step waits without a deadline for objects to settle; no live backend is declared or validated
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance the analytic step count only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the analytic world stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last observation and block layout stay readable
